title: set_thermal_parameters accepts house heat loss and thermal mass and changes nothing in two-zone
claim: With the two-zone model in force (the default 'auto' mode resolves to it, and 'on'), a set_thermal_parameters call raising house_heat_loss_coefficient 0.15 -> 0.35 kW/°C or lowering house_thermal_mass 10 -> 3 kWh/°C is acknowledged and stored but moves the published plan by 0.000 kW-steps, after the call and after a restart (4 of 4 two-zone cells), where the single-zone arm moves 167.6 and 5.9.
mechanism: The two-zone model reads the per-zone upper/lower floor heat loss and masses; the action writes ThermalParameters.heat_loss_coefficient / house thermal mass and the entry options, which no two-zone solve reads, and the action has no per-zone heat-loss field to write instead. Its own description promises two-zone support and its field help states the coefficient's effect without a zone condition; nothing refuses or warns.

evidence.unit: two-zone cells (mode x field) whose plan delta is 0.000 after the call and after a restart
evidence.contention_note: two other finder seats on the box; plan deltas are solver outputs at a frozen clock, contention-immune

perturbation.change: two_zone_mode: off in the entry data of every arm (config change): f02_two_zone_inert.py --perturb
perturbation.observed_value: inert cells 4 -> 0; plan delta 0.000 -> 167.619 (heat loss) and 5.882 (mass)

metric_definition: |sum of data['schedule'][i]['power'] after - before| for one set_thermal_parameters field, after the call and after a restart, per two-zone mode

null_control.note: single-zone: the same call moves the plan as documented

phenomenon_property: Every field set_thermal_parameters accepts changes the model the next solve uses in every zone mode it accepts the field in, or the call refuses/flags it in that mode.
reproduction_steps: Set up an entry with default two_zone_mode (auto)
Compare the plan before and after (and after a restart): identical
proposed_fix_scope: Either map the house fields onto the zone parameters in two-zone (scaling upper/lower floor heat loss and masses), or refuse them with a ServiceValidationError naming the per-zone fields, and add the per-zone heat-loss fields the options page has; field help says which mode reads which field.
